title: Popcorn stitch — the clean-edged raised cluster
subtitle: Complete trebles, not incomplete ones — the cluster faces you as you work
excerpt: Popcorn stitch is a group of five completed trebles worked into the same base stitch, then closed by threading the first stitch back through the last. The cluster pops toward you as you work — opposite to a bobble.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Vol. 5 (1890) — raised cluster groups in Aran-style crochet patterns.

glossaryTerms.definition: A cluster of five completed trebles all worked into the same base stitch, then the first stitch removed from the hook and pulled through the last to close the cluster. The group pops forward on the side facing you as you work.

heroPrompt: A swatch of popcorn stitch in aran-weight cream cotton, three popcorns per row visible with double crochet between, showing the defined round clusters facing outward, close-up on linen.

inlineDiagramTopics.description: Removing the hook from the last stitch and threading back through the first stitch to close

content.text: uses five completed trebles — not unfinished ones like the bobble. All five are worked into the same base stitch, then the first stitch is re-threaded through the last to pull the group into a tight round cluster. The cluster pops toward you as you work, which means you can work popcorns on right-side rows.
Work to the base stitch where the popcorn goes.
Work 5 complete trebles into the same base stitch. Each treble is worked in full — no leaving loops unfinished.
Remove the hook from the working loop. Do not let the loop unravel — hold it or park a stitch marker through it.
Insert the hook from front to back through the top of the first treble of the group (the first stitch worked).
Re-insert the hook into the held working loop and pull it through the top of the first treble. The five trebles gather into a round cluster facing you.
One chain to lock the cluster (optional but common in printed patterns). Continue the row.

attrs.title: Popcorn or bobble?
attrs.body: Popcorns give a rounder, more defined cluster than bobbles and face toward you as you work — no need to flip rows. They use more yarn per cluster than a bobble of the same height, and they stand up off the fabric more boldly. Choose popcorn for defined textured motifs; choose bobble for a lower-profile all-over texture.

items.symptom: Loop drops off the hook when removing it
items.cause: Not holding the working loop after removing the hook
items.fix: Park a stitch marker through the working loop as soon as the hook comes out. Pull the marker out once the hook is re-inserted.

items.cause: The five trebles were worked at different tensions
items.fix: Work all five trebles at the same even tension. Work them slightly looser than the surrounding stitches — the trebles need room to fan out before being gathered.

content.text: Star stitch creates a gathered shape using a different pulling method — five loops drawn into a single centre point. Crocodile stitch builds on the idea of working multiple stitches around a single post to create overlapping scale shapes.
